title: Port continuous batcher to coroutine runtime; add KV telemetry sandbox
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: The continuous batcher currently uses a hybrid callback/worker-thread model with several legacy synchronization points that amplify tail latency under mixed workloads. The existing code path also mixes synchronous IO and thread parking, which complicates our dependency upgrades (notably tokio and futures crates) and makes memory/heap pressure analysis noisy. Multiple incidents (Q4-2025) correlated by flamegraphs show long lock hold times inside the batch commit path and periodic KV cache churn when the batcher stalls.

Goal: Incrementally port the continuous batcher to an async coroutine-style runtime (async/await) to remove a class of thread parking paths, reduce allocations by reusing task stack buffers, and make the codebase ready for dependency upgrades (tokio 0.3 -> 1.x). Simultaneously introduce a lightweight KV telemetry sandbox to measure fine-grained metrics (per-shard hit/miss, eviction latency, lock hold time, allocation hotpaths) so we can validate behavior during canary rollouts. Targets: reduce p99 latency for continuous inference bursts by ~15%, reduce sys CPU by ~10%, and provide per-tenant KV observability for diagnosing regressions.

Approach: 1) Introduce a "coroutine adapter" crate (batcher_coroutine_adapter) that exposes the same public batcher API but is implemented via async/await tasks. The adapter will be behind a compile/runtime feature flag to allow safe rollback. 2) Keep the public KV store contract unchanged; implement a compatibility shim (kvcache_async_shim) that provides async-friendly interfaces while delegating to the existing on-disk/innermem store. 3) Add KV telemetry sandbox: an opt-in metrics layer that emits per-request and per-eviction traces to a dedicated metrics namespace (kvcache.sandbox.*). The sandbox will be gated behind a node-level config and limited retention to avoid billing/ingestion blowups. 4) Upgrade runtime dependencies in a separate commit: tokio -> 1.19, bytes -> 1.x, and futures -> 0.3.x; perform compilation with both the old and new adapter to validate ABI-like surface compatibility.

Testing & Validation: Build microbench harnesses that emulate realistic token-length mixes and cache locality. Run perf runs with flamegraphs, heap profiles (jemalloc), and lock contention metrics. Create a canary rollout plan on a low-traffic Dedicated pool with a short TTL canary (1 hour) and automated rollback on error-rate or latency regression thresholds.

Rollout Plan: 
- Phase 1 (dev): implement adapter and shim, unit + integration tests (this ticket).
- Phase 2 (staging): deploy sandbox-enabled adapter to staging, run long-run perf and chaos tests for 24-72h.
- Phase 3 (canary): enable on a small Dedicated shard with telemetry exported; monitor dashboards for 6 hours, then expand if stable.
- Phase 4: full rollout with gradual tenant ramp.

Risks & Mitigations: 
- Regression risk from dependency upgrades: keep changes scoped; dependency bump in separate PR and CI gate.
- Telemetry overhead: sandbox is opt-in and rate-limited; default off for production until proven low overhead.
- Subtle concurrency bugs: maintain the old path behind a feature flag for quick rollback and keep extensive unit testing around session handoff and preemption.

Why unique: Rather than a wholesale rewrite of scheduler internals, this ticket focuses on converting the batcher execution model to async/coroutines and pairing that change with an observability-focused KV sandbox so we can measure the real-world impact before touching global scheduler policies.
acceptance_criteria: Coroutine adapter compiles and passes unit tests behind feature flag
Compatibility shim preserves existing KV semantics (regression tests pass)
Microbench shows no >5% regression in mean latency and demonstrates p99 improvement in at least one workload profile
KV telemetry sandbox emits per-shard hit/miss and eviction latency metrics when enabled
Staging canary runs for 48h without SLO violations and rollouts documented in release notes
comments: 2026-03-02 - Arjun Patel: Initial prototype completed. Converted the smallest hot path (batch commit) to an async task and saw a 9% reduction in sys CPU in microbench. Pushed prototype to PR #1287 for early review.
2026-03-05 - Maya Chen (creator): Design review notes: PM asks for clear dashboard widgets for per-tenant KV health and a kill-switch wenn metrics ingestion spikes. Added dashboard task to follow-up.

2026-03-07 - Sofia Martinez (SRE): Reviewed canary plan; suggested adding a heap-fingerprint baseline using jemalloc stats to detect drift. Also flagged the tokio upgrade for a separate dependency PR to reduce review scope.

2026-03-11 - QA (Liam O'Connor): Integration tests found a race when a session is preempted and the task is dropped — leading to unflushed batch state in rare cases. Repro steps and a failing test added to PR. Marked 'Blocked' on that sub-case until fix landed.
2026-03-12 - Arjun Patel: Implemented graceful cancellation of in-flight batch tasks and added explicit drain on task drop; updated PR with fix and new unit tests. Re-running CI.
decisions: Use async/await coroutine model for the batcher runtime (feature-flagged) rather than incremental refactoring of the thread callback model
Keep KV store API contract stable; introduce async shim to avoid broad changes to storage layer
Separate dependency upgrade PR from adapter implementation to simplify bisecting regressions
notes: Baseline microbench: sustained throughput 1200 rps, median latency 18ms, p99 210ms (mixed token distribution)
Target after work: p99 <= 180ms on same harness and 10% lower system CPU
Telemetry budget: limit sandbox to 5% of sample traffic by default and 1k traces/min per node
